overall_summary: Bitcoin shows recovery by retaking 63000 but mixed catalysts leave direction unclear. Geopolitical tensions and ETF outflows offset potential regulatory support. Macro data stays neutral with no strong market driver.
key_points: Weekly ETF outflows continue despite rebound
Clarity Act vote eyed for July
Ukraine strike and China tariffs add risk

items.title: Bitcoin Retakes $63,000 Level After June Slide
items.summary: Bitcoin climbed back above 63,000 dollars, reversing losses from late June amid thin holiday trading volume. The move shows buyers defending key support after a weak period. Traders should watch whether it holds or breaks higher, as it could signal renewed momentum heading into the week.
items.impact: Supports short-term bullish bias if support holds.

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Post Weekly Outflows Despite Earlier Rebound
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of about 526 million dollars for the week, extending a recent negative streak even after a single-day inflow earlier in the period. Flows remain a key institutional sentiment gauge. Traders care because sustained outflows can pressure prices while inflows often provide support.
items.impact: Continued pressure on demand but not a new catalyst.

items.title: Clarity Act Final Draft Expected Soon as Senate Eyes July Vote
items.summary: The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act is advancing with expectations of a final Senate draft release and potential floor action after the July recess starting July 13. Lawmakers aim to clarify crypto regulation between SEC and CFTC. Traders should monitor this as positive regulatory clarity could unlock institutional flows and reduce uncertainty.
items.impact: Potential long-term positive catalyst for market structure.

items.title: US ISM Services PMI Hits 54.5 in June
items.summary: The Institute for Supply Management released its June services PMI at 54.5, showing continued expansion in the dominant US services sector. Readings above 50 signal growth, with details on business activity, new orders, and prices due at the 10 a.m. ET release. Traders watch this closely because strong services data supports a resilient economy, which can influence Fed rate expectations and risk assets like Bitcoin.
items.impact: Mixed signals on growth vs inflation could keep markets range-bound.

items.title: S&P Global US Services PMI Final at 51.3 for June
items.summary: S&P Global confirmed its final June services PMI at 51.3, slightly above flash estimates and showing modest expansion in business activity. The composite PMI also came in around 52.2. These figures matter for crypto traders as they gauge overall economic momentum ahead of key Fed decisions and can sway dollar strength or bond yields.
items.impact: In-line data likely limits big moves in DXY or yields today.

items.title: US Economic Calendar Focuses on Services Data Today
items.summary: With US markets returning after the July 4 holiday, attention turns to today's S&P and ISM services PMI releases plus other indicators like final PMIs. No major inflation or jobs data is due, but these reports provide fresh reads on economic health. Crypto traders should note any surprises, as they feed into broader macro sentiment and potential Fed path pricing.
items.impact: Data-dependent trading expected with limited catalysts.

items.title: Russian missiles and drones strike Kyiv, killing at least 10
items.summary: Russia launched a major overnight attack with ballistic missiles and drones on Ukraine's capital, killing at least 10 people and injuring dozens more. The strike comes just days ahead of a key NATO summit and highlights ongoing vulnerabilities in Ukrainian air defenses. Traders should watch for potential risk-off moves in markets as escalation in the Ukraine war raises geopolitical uncertainty.
items.impact: Heightens risk aversion and supports safe-haven flows

items.title: Trump holds 90-minute call with Putin, speaks to Zelenskyy
items.summary: President Trump spoke for nearly 90 minutes with Russian President Putin on July 4 and also called Ukraine's Zelenskyy, offering to help broker an end to the Ukraine war ahead of the NATO summit in Turkey. Both leaders discussed the conflict and agreed to continue talks at the summit. Any progress on de-escalation could ease some geopolitical premium in risk assets.
items.impact: Potential for reduced war-related uncertainty if talks advance

items.title: NATO summit in Turkey opens amid Ukraine and spending tensions
items.summary: The NATO summit begins in Ankara with leaders focused on the Ukraine war, European defense spending commitments, and questions over long-term US involvement in the alliance. Trump is attending and has pushed allies on burden-sharing. Outcomes could influence broader risk sentiment and energy markets.
items.impact: Unresolved outcomes may keep volatility elevated

items.title: US proposes new tariffs on Chinese imports amid labor probes
items.summary: The US Trade Representative is moving forward with proposed additional tariffs of 10-12.5 percent on Chinese goods and dozens of other partners following findings on forced labor issues. Comments close soon and hearings are scheduled, keeping trade policy in focus. Renewed tariff threats typically weigh on global growth expectations and risk assets.
items.impact: Adds pressure on equities and supports volatility

items.title: Iran ceasefire and sanctions relief remain in focus
items.summary: Ongoing diplomacy around the Iran ceasefire includes temporary sanctions lifts and safe passage provisions through the Strait of Hormuz. Any fresh developments could affect oil supply risks in the region. Traders monitor for signals on energy price stability.
items.impact: Limits immediate oil shock risk but keeps watch on Hormuz
